title: Lopburi to Phetchabun: 3-Day Road Trip, Old Town to Mountains | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night road trip across Lopburi and Phetchabun in Thailand: start in Lopburi's old town with monkeys and Khmer ruins, then drive up to Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek for morning sea fog. Real routes, drive times, and stops.

h1:
Lopburi to Phetchabun
From Old Town to the Mountains
intro: This route folds two worlds into one trip. You start in Lopburi's old town, with its monkeys, Khmer ruins, and an Ayutthaya-era palace, then drive north into Phetchabun for Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek, where the sea fog rolls in at dawn. We've laid it out as 3 days and 2 nights, self-driving at an easy pace with no rush.

blocks.html: Lopburi and Phetchabun sit on more or less the same line. Driving from Lopburi town up through Lam Narai and Phu Toei into Phetchabun takes about three and a half to four hours, so the two stitch together smoothly into one trip. You spend the first morning wandering the old town before it gets too hot, drive up the mountain in the afternoon, then catch the sea fog the next morning.

This plan works best if you're driving yourself, because public transport up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek is awkward. If you don't have a car, you can take a Lopburi–Lom Sak bus and then rent or charter a vehicle once you're in Phetchabun, but it's far easier with your own car.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Lopburi old town, then drive up to Phetchabun

blocks.html: Give the Lopburi old town the morning through midday. The main historical sites are close together and walkable. Hit the road north in the early afternoon and you'll reach Phetchabun around evening, just before dark, which beats driving up the mountain at night.

items.note: An 800-year-old Khmer Bayon-style temple, entry around 10 THB. Go early before the sun gets harsh. Lots of monkeys, so keep your valuables tucked away and take your glasses off if a monkey comes close.
Right next to Prang Sam Yot, just across the road, and free to enter. This is monkey central, with troops of several hundred. Make your wish, but watch out for monkeys snatching food bags.
A palace from the reign of King Narai, now the Somdet Phra Narai National Museum, entry around 30 THB. The grounds are shaded and leafy; allow about an hour to walk through.
Around Vichayen Road and the old-town market you'll find boat-noodle shops and local eats. Fuel up before the long drive.
The route runs Lopburi–Lam Narai–Phu Toei into Phetchabun, about three and a half to four hours of driving. There's a gas station near Lam Narai where you can stop for the restroom and to fill up.

items.activity: Arrive in Phetchabun town and check in
items.note: Staying in town the first night makes it easy to find dinner, then you head up Khao Kho the next morning. If you're up for it and there's still daylight, you can push straight up to Khao Kho instead.

blocks.title: About the Lopburi monkeys
blocks.html: The old-town monkeys are smart and quick. Don't carry plastic bags or food where they can see them, and keep your glasses, hat, and phone secure. If a monkey climbs onto your car, don't panic — just drive slowly and it'll hop off on its own.

blocks.text: Day 2 — A full day on Khao Kho

blocks.html: This is the heart of the trip. Khao Kho is cooler than the lowlands, with viewpoints, pretty temples, and mountain-view cafes lined up along the road as you climb. You can loop around and pick them off one at a time. If you want to catch the Phu Thap Boek sea fog the next morning, it's worth shifting your stay over toward the Phu Thap Boek side or near the access road tonight.

items.note: If you stayed in Phetchabun town, it's about an hour up to Khao Kho. The road has plenty of bends, so drive slowly and use a low gear on the way down. It takes some focus, but the views are worth it.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaew
items.note: A hilltop temple decorated with colorful tiles and ceramic bowls, looking out over the valley. It's one of Khao Kho's most popular photo spots. Dress modestly, and go early before the crowds build.
The road up Khao Kho is dotted with mountain-view cafes. Stop for a coffee and sit in the cool breeze; most coffees run about 60–120 THB. Pick a spot with an open view over the valley.

items.activity: Lunch + Thung Salaeng Luang National Park (if you have time)
items.note: Thung Salaeng Luang is a vast grassland park with campgrounds and viewpoints. If your day is packed you can skip it and just keep the stops you care about most.

items.activity: Drive on to Phu Thap Boek
items.note: From Khao Kho to Phu Thap Boek is about an hour and a half of driving, and the final stretch is very steep. If you've got a small, underpowered car, you can use a local truck service to ride up to the highest point. Best to arrive before dark.

items.activity: Check in at Phu Thap Boek and watch the sunset
items.note: Plenty of Phu Thap Boek stays have a view right from the bed. It gets cold tonight, so pack enough warm layers. On a clear night you'll see loads of stars.

blocks.title: Driving in the mountains
blocks.html: Some stretches of the climb up Phu Thap Boek are steep and narrow. Small sedans or drivers unfamiliar with the road should take care. If you're not confident, park at the bottom and hire a local truck up to the highest point — it's safer. Fill up your tank before heading up; gas stations on the mountain are hard to find.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Phu Thap Boek sea fog, then head home

blocks.html: On the last day you're up before dawn for the sea fog. Phu Thap Boek is the highest peak in Phetchabun, and from about 5 to 6 in the morning is the golden window when the fog hangs low over the valley. Once you've got your shots, have breakfast and ease into the drive home.

items.activity: Wake up for the sea fog
items.note: Set an alarm and get to a viewpoint near your stay before the sky lightens. The sea fog is at its best from late rainy season into early winter, and it gets very cold, so wear enough warm layers.

items.activity: Walk the Hmong market and grab breakfast
items.note: Near Phu Thap Boek there's a Hmong market selling cold-climate vegetables, strawberries (in season), and warm food. Good for grabbing some snacks to take back in the car.

items.activity: Stop at a vegetable farm / strawberry garden (in season)
items.note: In winter there are strawberry patches and cold-climate vegetable farms to stop and photograph. Out of season it's just regular vegetable plots, so check the season before you plan.
Use a low gear going down and don't ride the brakes. From Phu Thap Boek back to Lopburi or Bangkok, leave time for a rest stop along the way.

items.name: Don't-miss spots on the Lopburi side
items.blurb: Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan Shrine, and King Narai's Palace — all walkable within one neighborhood.

items.name: Don't-miss spots on the Phetchabun side
items.blurb: Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaew, the Khao Kho viewpoints, and the Phu Thap Boek sea fog at dawn.

blocks.text: Best time of year to go

items: November–February — winter, with the thickest sea fog and cool weather, but also the most crowds. Mountain stays fill up fast, so book ahead.
Late rainy into early winter (October) — plenty of fog and lush green hills, with fewer crowds than peak winter. A lot of people's favorite window.
Rainy season (June–September) — green and lush, with fog after the rain, but the mountain roads get slippery, so drive carefully. The sea fog comes and goes.
Hot season (March–May) — still cooler up the mountain than the lowlands, but less sea fog. Better for cafe-hopping and views than for chasing fog.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days, 2 nights)

items: Fuel + tolls — split among the car, roughly 1,500–2,500 THB per vehicle for the whole trip, depending on distance and the car.
2 nights of lodging — about 1,200–3,000 THB per person (one night in town + one up the mountain). Good views on Phu Thap Boek cost more.
Lopburi site entry fees — about 50 THB total (Prang Sam Yot ~10 + King Narai's Palace ~30).
Food + cafes — about 800–1,500 THB per person over the trip.
Rough total — about 3,500–6,000 THB per person if you split the car costs 3–4 ways.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Lopburi to Phetchabun?
faq.a: From Lopburi town up to Phetchabun via Lam Narai and Phu Toei takes about three and a half to four hours of driving. Set off in the early afternoon and you'll arrive before dark, so you won't have to drive up the mountain at night.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for this trip?
faq.a: It's far easier with a car, since public transport up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek is awkward. If you don't have one, take a Lopburi–Lom Sak bus first, then rent or charter a local vehicle once you're in Phetchabun.

faq.q: Where should I stay during the trip?
faq.a: Stay in Phetchabun town the first night for easy access to food. For the second night, shift over to the Phu Thap Boek or Khao Kho side so you can be up in time for the morning sea fog. In winter, mountain stays fill up fast, so book ahead.

faq.q: Can I drive a sedan up Phu Thap Boek?
faq.a: Some stretches of the climb up Phu Thap Boek are steep and narrow. Small sedans or drivers unfamiliar with the road should take care. If you're not confident, park at the bottom and hire a local truck up to the highest point — it's safer.

faq.q: When is the sea fog clearest?
faq.a: From late rainy season into winter, roughly October to February, is when the fog is thickest. The 5-to-6-a.m. window is the golden hour, when the fog hangs low over the valley.
